stages.title: Add isolated automated tests
stages.objective: Introduce a deterministic, non-interactive test command and meaningful regression coverage for src/cli.ts, src/config.ts, src/provider.ts, and src/workflow.ts.
completion_criteria: npm test executes actual assertions, exits after completion, and returns nonzero when an assertion fails.
Tests cover configuration defaults, overrides, invalid TOML and workflow values, and init overwrite protection.
Tests cover CLI help and version, argument errors, init and status behavior, and epic input handling through controlled workflow execution.
Tests cover provider invocation arguments and read-only permissions, JSON and event response parsing, subprocess failures, empty responses, and timeout handling.

Workflow tests cover repository preconditions, configured and discovered checks, stage dependencies, bounded failure attempts, persisted failure and resume state, read-only mutation restoration, and commit or push failure handling.

Provider sessions use controlled substitutes; filesystem and Git integration tests use disposable repositories and local remotes or mocks, require no credentials or network, and clean up their resources.
Lint and typecheck cover test code without adding test artifacts to the production build.
All local checks and the existing build pass, and README documents how to run the tests.

stages.title: Run PR checks and post-merge builds
stages.objective: Add GitHub Actions workflows that reuse the local commands for pull-request checks and build the resulting main branch revision after merge.
completion_criteria: Pull-request workflows install dependencies with npm ci and run lint, typecheck, and tests using the documented package scripts.
CI uses Node.js versions compatible with the declared runtime and verifies the Node.js 20 baseline.
Each failed quality command produces a failed CI result; checks require no provider credentials or external service sessions.
A push to main, including a merged pull request, triggers npm ci and npm run build for that revision.
The build verifies that dist/src/cli.js exists, is executable, and successfully handles --help or --version.
Workflow configuration and event filters are validated, and the exact CI commands pass from a clean installation.
README explains PR checks and the post-merge build; workflows use read-only repository permissions and add no publishing or deployment behavior.
